Amanda — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then Ive attached a redlineable private-offer template and an internal guidance note for your procurement team.

- Pricing cadence: AWS private offers can be structured as either an annualized committed spend with monthly invoicing or a fixed monthly charge drawn against the PO; we typically recommend annualized commits for better unit pricing.
- Term length: our standard options are 12, 24, and 36 months. Discounts tier at 12 (baseline), 24 (~7-12% band), 36 (~15-25% band) depending on committed $ and GPU capacity reservation.
- Buyer approvals: on the buyer side, AWS Marketplace requires the buyer to accept the private offer in the console and their procurement signatory to approve depending on their internal thresholds. On Redwood's side, discount approvals above 15% need signoff from Sales Ops + Finance; exceptions above 20% require VP Sales (vanessa) + Marketplace lead (karthik) approval.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ill send an internal one-pager to procurement that maps buyer approval thresholds -> expected signatures.
2) Vanessa — can you confirm the discount guardrails and whether we have authority to approve a 22% concession for strategic logos?
3) Amanda — if you can share an internal timeline for approvals (who signs and by when) well draft an offer that matches buyer acceptance requirements on AWS Marketplace.

Attached: Redwood_AWS_PO_Template.docx (private offer template), FastScale_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW stub).

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

Marcus — short answer on concessions: we can approve up to 15% discount at quota/AE level for standard T&Cs. Anything between 15-20% needs Sales Ops review (me) + Finance sign-off; >20% requires VP Sales review. For strategic proofs-of-value where we accept a steeper slope, we prefer a 24–36 month term and a minimum committed spend floor.

Notes for the offer:
- If they want a 36-month term with 20%+, we need a guaranteed monthly minimum (e.g., $25k/month) and an early termination clause tied to capacity decommit.
- For AWS private offers specifically: buyer must accept the offer in their AWS account; AWS sometimes requires the buyers billing owner + authorized signatory to approve for PO issuance. This can add 5-10 business days if they run it through their centralized procurement portal.

Karthik — please flag any marketplace policy wrinkles on acceptance/signing cadence.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 11:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FastScale interest in private offer — term length + buyer approval questions

Looping in AWS rep notes I received earlier:
- AWS private offers can be configured to require the buyer to accept via the Marketplace console; the acceptance record and timestamp are stored in AWS. For buyer approval flows, encourage customers to add the Marketplace "accept offer" step to their procurement checklist to avoid delays.
- DocuSign/External signature flows: Marketplace still requires the buyer to click accept; attaching a DocuSign to collect signatures in parallel is fine, but the PO isn't "consumable" until the buyer accepts in AWS.
- For co-sell eligibility: offers with >25% discount are reviewable by AWS for co-sell attribution; keep a co-sell carve-out conversation with the ISC to ensure co-sell credit if applicable.

I recommend we draft two variants for FastScale: 24-month (10–12% discount) and 36-month (18–22% discount with $25k/mo minimum). Marcus, I can help prepare the AWS-side acceptance checklist for Amanda so procurement knows exactly who needs to click what.

— Karthik
Marketplace Partnerships Lead | Redwood Inference
